actionableSelection.ruleDetail: GO-ACT-1 (provider-authored, Claude Code): actionableSelection = mission-priority-selector.selectNextExplained over the SAME register candidates and options, with every item lacking an AUTHORIZED next step mapped to the non-selectable status NOT_AUTHORIZED_NOW (excluded with its reason; still counted for dependency/unblock edges) — no new scoring, same ties semantics. An item has an AUTHORIZED next step iff it is not owner-gated (requiresOwnerAuthorization) AND (its WORK_ITEM_CONTRACT is AUTHORIZED with authorizedBy, OR odg-authorization-scope derives its CURRENT step authorized). PROPOSED is never authorized. Applied only when the strategic decision chose an item (SELECTED/TIE_EXPLAINED) that is itself not actionable; DECISION_REQUIRED stays a halt. Dispatch still only through the existing NATIVE + isolated path; provider/docs steps are reported, not dispatched.

dispatchTarget.rule: GO-DT-1 (provider rule): a scoped execution step is dispatched only to contract.authorization.dispatchTargets[step] = { command, args?, writeSet } (command + writeSet ⊆ WORK_ITEM_CONTRACT.write_set, repo-relative, no '..'); absent/invalid ⇒ NO_DISPATCH_TARGET fail-closed, never a fallback to odg-run <id>; plain AUTHORIZED contracts keep the existing odg-run path. LIMIT (stated, not hidden): the target runs on the host (not under bwrap — the provider-sandbox profile cannot bind the /home scratch + node_modules without widening its confidential-prefix guard), so only writes INSIDE the scratch are confined (git status --ignored, every entry ⊆ target writeSet, pristine scratch required); out-of-scratch writes ($HOME, /tmp, main repo) are NOT confined ⇒ dispatch is fail-closed by default (UNSANDBOXED_TARGET_NOT_OPTED_IN) and runs only with the explicit opt-in allowUnsandboxedTarget (CLI --allow-unsandboxed-target), recorded in the trace

dispatchTimeout.rule: GO-DTO-1 (provider rule): plain odg-run dispatch ⇒ 600000 ms. A contract-declared scoped target ⇒ from WORK_ITEM_CONTRACT.preRegistration.caps: (a) caps absent, or neither maxRunWallMs nor perTrialWallMs declared ⇒ 600000; (b) maxRunWallMs declared ⇒ maxRunWallMs + margin; (c) else perTrialWallMs × trials + margin, trials = (|dataset.replication| + |dataset.heldOut|) × |keys(arms)| × |decoding.seeds| (an UPPER bound of the rows the runner may execute — every arm on every task at every seed); trials not derivable ⇒ the ceiling (conservative: a capped run is bounded by its own caps and is never killed early); (d) a declared wall cap (maxRunWallMs / perTrialWallMs) that is not a finite positive number ≤ Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER (negative, string, NaN, null, 1e300 …) ⇒ dispatch REFUSED, code GO-DTO-1_MALFORMED_CAPS (fail-closed like GO-DT-1); a valid but huge result ⇒ clamped to the ceiling. Value = Math.ceil(result) (the exact integer odg-go.ts must use; any mismatch there ⇒ refused). Cycle deadline: when a declared target will be dispatched, effectiveDeadline = max(requested deadline, timeout + 300000) (the 300000 margin covers the steps before and after EXECUTE; elapsed-at-EXECUTE recorded) — extended, never refused, even over an explicit --deadline-ms (recorded): the dispatch is already bounded by its own timeout ≤ the ceiling, and a DEADLINE stop after it would only discard the EVIDENCE/NEXT_SELECTION of a run that already happened. results floored at 600000 (never below the plain timeout); margin 120000 ms; HARD CEILING 43200000 ms (12 h) never exceeded. Timeout kill semantics unchanged (SIGKILL ⇒ EXECUTED_FAIL; writes-confinement check still applied). The dispatch runs as its own process group (detached); timeout, STOP file, SIGTERM/SIGINT to GO or ODG_SCHEDULER_STOP=1 ⇒ SIGTERM to the group, 10 s grace, SIGKILL to the group, group exit awaited before the writes-confinement check
